projects.title: Vulnerability Intelligence Dashboard
projects.problem: Security teams at Citi had to manually query three separate vulnerability scanners — Snyk, Blackduck, and Checkmarx — each with paginated APIs returning hundreds of pages of results. The full fetch took ~6 minutes, making real-time security visibility impossible.
projects.approach: Architected a unified dashboard with asynchronous service orchestration and a worker-pool pattern. Three vulnerability streams ran in parallel, each processing paginated issue-detail calls concurrently. Results were aggregated into a single normalised view.
projects.outcome: Data-fetch time dropped from ~6 minutes to under 750ms. Presented the POC to senior leadership, resulting in multiple team onboarding requests.

projects.title: Release Planner — 25K+ Entry Retrieval
projects.problem: Release planning for 25K+ entries was a slow, manual process with response times around 2 minutes — making iterative planning impractical.
projects.approach: Built 15+ APIs with parallel fetching, in-memory caching, debouncing to reduce redundant calls, and pagination to manage payload size. Designed the data model for efficient lookup rather than full scans.
projects.outcome: Response time reduced from ~2 minutes to under 20ms — a 6000x improvement. The tool became the go-to release planning interface for the team.

projects.title: Commercial Acquisition — Eureka Service Discovery Migration
projects.problem: Manual routing configuration across APIM, Platform Security Gateway and 4 microservices caused high API latency (~1s overhead) and made adding new services a high-effort, error-prone process.

projects.title: Credit Unlock — First-in-Industry Capability

projects.title: SciBERT NLP Pipeline — Electrocatalyst Discovery
projects.problem: Manual literature review of scientific papers for electrocatalyst discovery was slow and unscalable. Researchers needed automated extraction of material properties and activity predictions from abstracts.
projects.approach: Fine-tuned SciBERT (domain-adapted BERT for scientific text) on 1.8M+ abstracts from Elsevier and Springer. Applied representation learning to encode material descriptors and predict catalytic activity.
projects.outcome: Published in a peer-reviewed journal. 4 citations to date. The pipeline demonstrated that NLP could surface material candidates from literature at a scale manual review cannot match.

projects.title: RL-Based DVFS on Raspberry Pi 4B
projects.problem: Conventional DVFS operates at the OS scheduler level, reacting to load but unable to anticipate thermal and power constraints or optimise beyond pre-defined frequency steps.
projects.approach: Designed a custom RL environment wrapping the Raspberry Pi's DVFS interface. Trained an RL agent to learn a control policy that balances performance, power draw, and thermal state — operating at a layer below the kernel scheduler.
projects.outcome: Demonstrated that RL can extend DVFS optimisation beyond scheduler-level heuristics on real embedded hardware, with measurable thermal and power benefits.

systemDesigns.title: Salesforce Marketing Cloud Migration — Kafka Event Architecture
systemDesigns.context: Live migration from Cheetah-based email triggering to Salesforce Marketing Cloud for Consumer Credit Servicing. Required zero data loss during cutover, consistency across two DBs (FusionDB as source of truth), and no downtime.

decisions.question: Why Kafka over direct API calls for email triggering?
decisions.answer: Kafka provides durability and replay capability. Direct API calls to SFMC would create tight coupling and risk event loss on downstream failures. Kafka decouples producers from SFMC, enables retry without re-triggering upstream, and gives an auditable event log across the migration window.

decisions.question: Why retain FusionDB as source of truth during migration?
decisions.answer: Dual-write to both FusionDB and SFMC during migration creates a consistency risk. By keeping FusionDB as the authoritative source and only using SFMC as the delivery channel, we eliminated the risk of split-brain state and could roll back SFMC integration without data loss.

decisions.question: Why an Async MDC Executor for tiny-URL generation and payload construction?
decisions.answer: Tiny-URL generation and FusionDB payload construction are IO-bound and independent. An Async MDC Executor parallelises these operations while preserving MDC context for distributed tracing across async boundaries — critical for Splunk correlation in production.

systemDesigns.title: Commercial Acquisition — Netflix Eureka + APIM Migration
systemDesigns.context: 4 microservices behind APIM and Platform Security Gateway using manual routing tables. Goal: reduce latency, eliminate manual routing config, and enable AWS migration. Constraints: zero downtime, live traffic throughout.

decisions.question: Why Netflix Eureka over a static service registry or AWS Cloud Map?
decisions.answer: Eureka was already part of the Spring Cloud ecosystem in use, minimising library overhead. It provides client-side load balancing via Ribbon (integrated with Spring), self-registration, and health-check driven deregistration — all without requiring AWS-specific tooling at a stage when AWS migration hadn't started.

decisions.question: Why redesign APIM routing instead of just adding Eureka alongside existing config?
decisions.answer: Layering Eureka on top of existing manual routing would create dual maintenance — any new service would need both a routing table update and Eureka config. A clean break to dynamic discovery meant future onboarding required only Eureka registration, enabling true plug-and-play.

systemDesigns.title: Vulnerability Intelligence Dashboard — Async Aggregation
systemDesigns.context: Aggregate vulnerability data from Snyk, Blackduck and Checkmarx — each with paginated REST APIs returning hundreds of pages. Target: sub-second fetch for a unified dashboard. No dedicated message queue budget.

decisions.question: Why worker-pool processing over a simple parallel stream?
decisions.answer: Each vulnerability source had different rate limits and page depths. A fixed parallel stream would saturate slower sources or under-utilise faster ones. Worker pools with per-source thread budgets allowed independent tuning of concurrency per source, preventing one slow scanner from blocking the others.

decisions.question: Why not cache all results and serve from cache?
decisions.answer: Vulnerability data changes frequently — a stale cache would give a false sense of security. Instead, we optimised the fetch pipeline itself to be fast enough that caching wasn't needed for UX, while still being accurate at query time.

productionIncidents.title: 100K Erroneous Requests — Apigee Migration
productionIncidents.diagnosis: Correlated Splunk IP-level traffic logs and API timelines across the migration window. Identified two distinct root causes: browser-tab reload storms generating duplicate requests, and malformed bot POST traffic that bypassed validation post-migration.
productionIncidents.fix: Deployed an overnight fix targeting both traffic patterns. Added request deduplication logic and tightened bot traffic filtering at the gateway layer.
productionIncidents.impact: 2xx success rate restored to 99.82% by the next morning. Zero escalation to leadership.

productionIncidents.title: Race Condition — Shared Static State Mutation
productionIncidents.diagnosis: Traced intermittent request contamination to shared static state being mutated across concurrent threads. The unsafe access pattern caused one request's data to bleed into another's, with restarts as the only recovery mechanism.
productionIncidents.fix: Replaced shared-state access with deep-copy isolation at the point of object creation, ensuring each request thread operated on its own copy.
productionIncidents.impact: Eliminated restart-based recovery. Zero recurrence after fix deployment.

productionIncidents.title: Cross-DC Traffic Failure — 1 Week vs. 1 Month
productionIncidents.diagnosis: Traced deployment blocker to cross-DC traffic failures spanning GRN, DMZ, APIM and Akamai layers. Each layer appeared healthy in isolation — the failure was at the intersection of routing rules across all four.
productionIncidents.fix: Coordinated with the Akamai team to identify and update conflicting routing rules. Validated end-to-end traffic flow across all DC hops before deployment.
productionIncidents.impact: Unblocked and delivered production deployment within 1 week against a proposed 1-month delay.

productionIncidents.title: iOS Autofill Validation Failure
productionIncidents.diagnosis: Traced an edge-case validation failure to iOS-specific autofill behaviour that populated form fields in a different order and format than desktop browsers, triggering a validation path the desktop code never hit.
productionIncidents.fix: Corrected the validation handler to normalise input regardless of fill source, and added iOS-specific integration test coverage.
productionIncidents.impact: iOS autofill flows unblocked for all affected customers.

productionIncidents.title: POS Email O(N) → O(1) Performance Fix
productionIncidents.diagnosis: POS approval-email processing was iterating nested JSON across 100+ credit-unit configurations to find the right template — an O(N) scan on every email triggered.
productionIncidents.fix: Replaced nested-JSON iteration with a pre-built direct lookup structure (map keyed by credit-unit ID), reducing per-email processing to O(1).
productionIncidents.impact: Email processing time dropped proportionally to configuration count. No further performance degradation as credit-unit count grows.

productionIncidents.title: Paperless Enrollment — SMS De-enrolment Bug
productionIncidents.diagnosis: A preference-update mutation in the paperless enrollment flow was overwriting the entire channel preference object rather than merging it. Enabling email reset all other channels to their default (off) state.
productionIncidents.fix: Corrected the update logic to perform a field-level merge, preserving existing channel preferences when updating a single channel.
productionIncidents.impact: Customer channel preferences preserved correctly. No customer data loss.
